workarounds.note: the chapter line is placed VIGNETTE.height + 6 mm below the top of the container and the summary hangs from it, so neither is anchored below #vignette. An image element reserves no height, and texts anchored to it are measured without the picture above them: without minHeight, chapter I's text would start 62 mm from the top of the page, inside the drawing (gotcha opener-image-no-reserve)
the frontispiece style sets span: 'page' in a one-column book: kept in its column, the sky field anchored to the page is cut at the 22 mm top margin (gotcha opener-clipped-at-top)

centred tracked labels (the title page's kicker and author, the running heads, the chapter line) move right by half their tracking, trail(), because 1.4.1 counts the tracking after the last letter when it centres a design text
headings.levels[0].breakBefore is restated with parity 'any': the headings object, there to name Fredericka the Great so that Open Sans is not loaded, drops the default H1 break

col() writes the hex beside each paletteId, because 1.4.1 paints the title page, opener and folio elements from the hex; bodyText.referenceColor is set in ink although the book cites nothing, because the palette does not reach it and it would stay #295AA3 (gotcha palette-skips-designs)

the chapter line and the summary give lineHeight as a multiple of their size (1 and 1.38), never pt(): a Dimension drops the opener's reservation, minHeight included (gotcha design-lineheight-multiple)
locale is 'it', the exact code of the bundled Italian patterns
every frontmatter value is quoted: title, subtitle and author print on the title page and in the verso running head

Collodi's dialogue dashes, di legno and in piedi are tied with U+00A0, which 1.4.1 holds only in paragraphs without inline marks; the one tied paragraph with an italic run (*ohi*, set on the rich path, where a no-break space can still break) was checked on the capture: its four ties fall mid-line or at the paragraph's end

what.en: Le avventure di Pinocchio (1883): chapter I and the opening of chapter II with Collodi’s chapter summaries, from the 1902 Bemporad edition, with typographic apostrophes, dashes and ellipses; chapter I’s summary has the comma after “falegname” that the edition’s table of contents prints and its chapter head leaves out
what.es: Le avventure di Pinocchio (1883): el capítulo I y el comienzo del II con los sumarios de Collodi, según la edición Bemporad de 1902, con apóstrofos, rayas y puntos suspensivos tipográficos; el sumario del capítulo I lleva, como el índice de la edición, la coma tras «falegname» que falta al comienzo del capítulo

what.en: The frontispiece: Tuscan hills, a hill village and a donkey cart of firewood on its way to the carpenter’s workshop
what.es: El frontispicio: colinas toscanas, un pueblo en lo alto y un carro de leña tirado por un asno camino del taller del carpintero

what.en: Chapter I’s vignette: Maestro Ciliegia, axe raised over the talking log
what.es: La viñeta del capítulo I: Maestro Ciliegia, con el hacha en alto sobre el tronco que habla

what.en: Chapter II’s vignette: Geppetto in his yellow wig receives the log, beside a pot of polenta
what.es: La viñeta del capítulo II: Geppetto, con su peluca amarilla, recibe el tronco junto a una olla de polenta
